title: Auth: magic-link sign-in dispatches through tenant-aware sender
journey: Pre-seed a status='verified' email_domains row (e2e-verified.example.com) for the franchisee's org so the tenant route exists
Logged out, open /sign-in-link — the 'Sign in by email' magic-link form renders
Type franchisee@gmail.com into the Email field
Observe the result toast surface in the notifications region ('Failed to send sign-in link' — see verification note on why this is the expected sandbox outcome)
verification: Server-side routing is the actual assertion and is captured in e2e-web/videos/test-5-server-log-proof.txt: the stack shows Object.sendMagicLink -> dispatchAuthEmail (better-auth.ts:173) -> sendTenantEmail (email-send-tenant.ts:178) running FIRST (tenant route), then on Resend rejection dispatchAuthEmail (better-auth.ts:196) -> sendMagicLinkEmail (email.ts:595) running SECOND (platform fallback). Both legs fire in order. The end Resend rejection (and thus the 'Failed to send sign-in link' UI toast) is a Resend sandbox limit — sandbox only delivers to the account owner and won't send from an un-DNS-verified domain — not a routing bug. The green-success leg needs a real DNS-verified domain and is deferred.
